title: SD: system suite — test/system/observation-feed.test.js fails on clean main (not host-related, cause unknown)
description:
## Problem

`test/system/observation-feed.test.js` fails under `npm run test:system`: the observation-feed system test. After a run completes, `feed.active` is not empty, so a completed run is reported as in flight (assertion `a completed run is not "in flight"`, `test/system/observation-feed.test.js:28`).

## Why it matters

The Observation feed is what operators read to see what is running. A completed run shown as in flight is either a real feed bug or Harbour changing the shape the test reads. The system suite is also the only place these behaviours are exercised end to end, and nothing automated watches it.

## Reproduces on

Repo: **JKershaw/simple-dispatcher**. `npm run test:system` (not in CI; `ci.yml` runs only `npm test`), with `HARBOUR_DIR` pointing at a LinearViewer checkout. Measured by LIN-4181 (merged as PR #309, `11a1279`) on the runner host:

* identical on clean `main` (`0992f39`) and on the LIN-4181 head, run from a workspace clone, a checkout in `/private/tmp`, and a checkout with `TMPDIR` inside `state/`;
* identical against Harbour `9e397e6b`, `10b2c82f` and `0dc1620e`;
* each also fails when its file is run on its own.
  So it is **not** host or location noise, **not** Harbour-version skew and **not** a LIN-4181 regression. The cause is **not known**: LIN-4181 triaged it only far enough to rule those out.

## Acceptance

* The cause is found and stated on this ticket: a real Simple Dispatcher defect, a real Harbour defect (then a Harbour ticket exists), or drift between the test and Harbour.
* `test/system/observation-feed.test.js` passes against the Harbour checkout it is run with, **or** is skipped with a stated, checked reason. It is not loosened to pass: the assertion on line 28 keeps guarding what it guards.
* `npm run test:system` no longer lists `observation-feed` among its failures, run from a workspace clone, with the other three named failures treated separately.

## Anchors

* `test/system/observation-feed.test.js:28`
* `test/system/harness/harbour.js` (how Harbour is started), `test/system/README.md`
* Related: LIN-2471 (an earlier, different red case in the same suite), LIN-4181 (found this; the triage is in its review comments and close-out)

## Unvalidated idea

None worth stating: the cause is unknown. A first step is to run this file alone with Harbour's logs kept and look at what the queue/feed holds at the failing assertion.

---

*Priority: priorityLevel 2 (Medium): wrong data on a read-only operator view, no control path; cause unknown; suite not in CI. Label: Bug (the workspace catalog has no narrower type label).*

## How to go about it (from a Survey before work began)

Two Surveys at simple-dispatcher `7d515d3` (on LIN-4150) found the cause by running this test alone on the new harness:

* **It's drift, not a defect.** Harbour LIN-3983 (`d3f67854`, #2171, 26 Oct) deliberately moved the Sessions view onto the 24-hour recency rule (`routes/dashboard-feed.js` `splitSessionsFeed`: "a session finished within a day is Active") and rewrote its own unit test to match.
* So `observation-feed.test.js:28` guards a contract Harbour retired. Run alone against Harbour `2ee4e600`: the run is there, `terminal: true`, `status: done`, in `active`; `recent` is empty.
* Every Harbour SHA this ticket lists already contains `d3f67854`, which is why "no version skew" didn't find it.
* **LIN-4188 is probably the same cause.** `tap1-openrouter.test.js:51-55` waits for the terminal session in `feed.recent` only.

### Scope decision (4 Nov, about 17:30 UTC)

John asked Claude to take the human's role in this process and choose a large enough option.

**Ruling: drift.** LIN-3983 was deliberate, so SD's test follows Harbour; no Harbour ticket.

**Scope: the larger option.** Of the four "cause unknown" system reds LIN-4181 filed, LIN-4185 and LIN-4186 also turned out to be contract drift ("the halt tests follow LIN-4079"), and this is the third. So the missing record of *which Harbour contract each scenario relies on* has already cost three tickets of hunting:

1. **Re-state the assertion as the new contract.** The LOCAL-1 session is `terminal: true` (and `status: done`, `waiting: false`) wherever the recency split puts it. Add a second assertion that `active`/`recent` follow the recency rule, so the test witnesses the contract Harbour actually has. Say plainly in the PR that line 28's guard moved from the bucket to the session, so it doesn't read as loosening.
2. **One helper** in the harness (`world.js` or `harbour.js`) that finds a session across `active ∪ recent`. Both `observation-feed` and `tap1-openrouter` use it, so "where does a terminal session live" exists once.
3. **LIN-4188 is in scope.** Check it first. If the same change turns it green, fix it here and close LIN-4188 with the evidence. If not, say why on LIN-4188 and leave it.
4. **Move the leftovers together:** the README gotcha and the `w.sessions` description (`test/system/README.md`), the KNOWN_RED entries in `harness/baseline-report.js` and their pinned list in `test/baseline-report.test.js`, and `docs/testing-and-ci.md:192`. Cite Harbour LIN-3983 by SHA.
5. **A contract note on every system scenario:** at the top of each `test/system/*.test.js`, one line naming the Harbour route or behaviour it pins, and the Harbour change that would break it. Add the convention to `test/system/README.md`, and a cheap census test that fails on a scenario file without the note. This is what turns the next drift from "red, cause unknown" into "Harbour changed X".

**At merge (we'll check it):**

* `npm run test:baseline` on a clean `main` shows `observation-feed` (and `tap1-openrouter`, if in scope) green;
* KNOWN_RED no longer lists them, with its unit test updated;
* no stale "running-only" wording remains;
* one session-finding helper;
* every system scenario carries a contract note, enforced by the census.

**Not this task's:** a Harbour-side contract test for the Sessions feed shape, and the baseline report naming *which* contract moved.

---

## Implementation Plan

*Pruned at close-out (2026-11-04): the plan was implemented as approved and merged in [https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/324](<https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/324>) (squash commit* `d8d186c`*, branch head* `f82cbe3`*). The one deviation from the plan's list:* `w.findSession` *on the world is a thin wrapper that no test calls (both feed tests call* `findSession(feed, ...)` *directly, because* `observation-feed` *needs the feed for the recency oracle); review accepted that. Close-out added the* `d3f67854` *SHA citation the plan asked for (3 places). The full plan text is preserved in the task snapshots (pre-prune snapshot captured 2026-11-04T17:47Z) and the decisions, witnesses and verification are in the comment trail.*

**fits one session.**

plan-review due: no

comments.body: Seen again during LIN-4220's review (PR #318, merged as 52d2c3d): this test still fails under `npm run test:system` on clean main @ 502901c and on the PR head, with the same failure name on both ("a completed standalone run appears as a terminal session…"), against Harbour eb44eff9. It is not a regression from #318. No change to this ticket's scope; recorded as a further data point.

LIN-4222 (PR https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/320, merged as 3330526) found this test failing identically on `main` @ `90bbf82` and on its own head: the same failure as named here, with the same pinned LinearViewer checkout (`eb44eff9`). It is not caused by the port change. Run alone it fails the same way. Linked as related; no new ticket filed. LIN-4224's scripted baseline should list this test as known-red until this ticket closes.

PR: https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/324 (branch `feat/lin-4187-sessions-feed-contract`, commit 69608ea). Not merged; merge is for review.

**Cause: drift, not a defect.** Harbour LIN-3983 (`d3f67854`) moved the Sessions feed to a 24h recency split (`splitSessionsFeed`): a run finished within the day is in `active`. `observation-feed.test.js:28` still asserted the retired running-only bucket. No Harbour ticket (deliberate change).

**What the PR does**
- observation-feed: the guard moves from the bucket to the session (`terminal`, `status: done`, `waiting: false`), plus a recency oracle over active/recent. Stated in the PR as a move, not a loosening.
- one helper `findSession` (harness/harbour.js), used by both feed tests; throws on double-listing or ambiguous match.
- LIN-4188 is fixed by the same lookup (see its comment).
- KNOWN_RED emptied; mechanism kept and tested on a fixture.
- Contract note on all 27 `test/system/*.test.js`, enforced by `test/system-contract-census.test.js`.
- Docs (system README, testing-and-ci) updated.

**Evidence**
- Before (clean main `7d515d3`, run alone): line 28 `1 !== 0`.
- After (branch): observation-feed and tap1 green run alone; `npm test` 4277 tests, 4272 pass, 0 fail, 5 skipped; `npm run test:system` 127 pass, 0 fail.
- Mutations (restored): reversed recency oracle fails observation-feed; removing the double-listing guard fails session-finder.
- CI on PR #324: `unit tests` SUCCESS.

**Not done here:** Harbour's own comment in `routes/dashboard-feed.js` still says "running-only split" (Harbour-side, out of scope). Merge check on clean main (`npm run test:baseline`) runs after merge.

## Review — LIN-4187

Reviewed PR https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/324 at head `69608ea` (base `7d515d3`), against LinearViewer `d7ceb373` (current; it contains LIN-3983 `d3f67854`).

CI: green. `unit tests` on `69608ea` passed. The system suite is not in CI, so I ran it on both branches myself (below).

**Cause confirmed from Harbour source.** It is drift, not a defect. `routes/dashboard-feed.js:684-703`: `splitSessionsFeed` (sessions view) puts taken sessions in `active` when `Number.isFinite(t) && now - t <= STALE_AFTER_MS`, with `t = Date.parse(lastActivity)` and 24h from `dashboard-session-state.js:23`, regardless of terminal state. The test's `withinDay` oracle copies this rule exactly, edge and NaN handling included.

**Scope against the plan.** All five decisions were carried out, and the changed files match the plan's places:
- Guard moved to the session: `terminal` / `status: 'done'` / `waiting: false`, plus the recency oracle. There is no `active.length` freeze and no clock hack.
- One `findSession` in `harness/harbour.js`, used by both `observation-feed` and `tap1-openrouter`. It throws on a double-listing and on an ambiguous match.
- LIN-4188 was checked first. It is the same cause, and its run-summary assertions pass after the fix.
- KNOWN_RED is empty. The mechanism is kept and tested on a fixture list.
- 27/27 scenario files carry a `// Contract: … Breaks if: …` line, and the census enforces it. I spot-read 6 notes (`halt-mechanism`, `harbour-ports`, `credential-rearm`, `happy-path`, `close-on-done`, `observation-feed`); each matches what its file exercises.
- No stale "running-only" wording is left in SD. The only "in flight" mention is the explanatory comment at `observation-feed.test.js:41-42`.

The PR merges cleanly onto current `main` (`44ab30e`), and `main` has not touched any of the PR's files since the base.

**Regression check.** `git log` on the changed files shows nothing reverted or re-applied. The `harbour.js` change only adds code. LIN-4224's KNOWN_RED labelling and summary still work and are still tested, now with fixture entries.

**Two-branch run (system suite, my run, same host, same Harbour):**
- head `69608ea`: `npm run test:system` → 127 tests, 127 pass, 0 fail.
- base `7d515d3`: 127 tests, 125 pass, 2 fail:
  - `a completed standalone run appears as a terminal session…` (renamed on head)
  - `generating a run summary drives Harbour's real OpenRouter client to the fake`
- No test passes on base and fails on head.
- `npm test` on head: 4277 tests, 4272 pass, 0 fail, 5 skipped.

**Mutation checks (each reverted, tree clean afterwards):**
1. Harbour `splitSessionsFeed` set back to the old running-only split (`active = !terminal`). `observation-feed` goes red on the oracle. `tap1-openrouter` stays green, as it should, because the helper finds the session in either bucket.
2. `findSession` double-listing guard disabled: `session-finder` has 2 failures.
3. `findSession` ambiguity guard disabled: `session-finder` has 1 failure.
4. Contract line removed from `boot.test.js`: the census fails and names `boot.test.js`.

**Class check.** The class is "a system test reads a single Sessions-feed bucket". It has exactly two members, `observation-feed` and `tap1-openrouter`, and both are fixed. A grep for `.recent` / `.active` / `sessionsFeed` / `w.sessions` finds no other feed reader. The Harbour comment still saying "running-only split" belongs to Harbour and is **outside** this ticket (the ticket names it as not this task's).

**Findings for close-out to fix (small, docs only):**
1. **SHA not cited (inside: scope item 4, "Cite Harbour LIN-3983 by SHA").** `d3f67854` appears nowhere in SD. Change `LIN-3983` to `LIN-3983, d3f67854` in three places:
   - the Sessions-feed gotcha in `test/system/README.md` (~line 127)
   - the known-red paragraph in `docs/testing-and-ci.md` (~line 195)
   - the `STALE_AFTER_MS` comment in `test/system/observation-feed.test.js` (~line 19)
2. Note only, no change required: `w.findSession` in `world.js:132` is documented in the README as the way to look a session up, but no test calls it. Both feed tests call `findSession(feed, …)` directly, because `observation-feed` needs the feed for the oracle. It is a two-line wrapper over the tested pure function, so I'm leaving it.

### What CI Did Not Prove
- **Inside (the acceptance criterion "`npm run test:baseline` on clean `main` no longer lists observation-feed", and scope item 3 for tap1):** the system suite is not in CI. My two-branch run above stands in for it. Its limits: same host, not a clean environment; only commit `69608ea`; one run each, so flaky failures can't be told apart from real ones. **Before close:** after merge, run `npm run test:baseline` on clean `main` from a workspace clone. Correct if `observation-feed.test.js` and `tap1-openrouter.test.js` both pass and no `known-red` line is printed. Wrong if either fails.
- **Inside (the recency rule, decision 1's stated limit):** the `recent` side of the oracle is witnessed only over whatever the feed holds. In this harness `recent` is always empty, so `!withinDay` is never exercised against a real aged session. This is the accepted, stated limit: Harbour's own LIN-3983 unit test covers that side, and a clock hack is ruled out. Settled by the stated limit; nothing to run.
- **Inside (the LIN-4188 close):** settled by the same post-merge `test:baseline` check. Close LIN-4188 with that output.

### Verdict
Approve — conditional on close-out discharging the ledger

The cause is confirmed, the guard was moved to the session rather than loosened, mutation checks show the tests catch the right failures, and the two-branch run shows both reds fixed with no new ones. Remaining: the post-merge `test:baseline` check and the one-line SHA citation fix.

## Close-out — LIN-4187

**Merged:** https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/324, squash commit `d8d186c`, pinned with `--match-head-commit f82cbe3`. Cause: drift, not a defect. Harbour LIN-3983 (`d3f67854`) moved the Sessions feed to a 24h recency split. `observation-feed`'s line-28 guard moved from the bucket to the session (`terminal`, `status: done`, `waiting: false`, in exactly one bucket), plus a recency oracle; this is a move, not a loosening. One `findSession` helper serves both feed tests, `KNOWN_RED` is empty (mechanism kept and tested on fixtures), all 27 `test/system/*.test.js` carry a `// Contract: … Breaks if: …` line enforced by a census, and the docs follow.

**Changes I made at close-out** (review finding 1, "SHA not cited"; docs and comment only, no assertion or behaviour change):
- `f82cbe3`: `LIN-3983` → `LIN-3983, d3f67854` in `test/system/README.md` (Sessions-feed gotcha), `docs/testing-and-ci.md` (known-red paragraph) and the `STALE_AFTER_MS` comment in `test/system/observation-feed.test.js`.
- Review's note 2 (`w.findSession` unused by tests) needed no change, as review said.

**CI:** CI exists (`unit tests`). It was green on the original head `69608ea`, and I re-established it on the new head `f82cbe3`: the run reported `completed success` before I merged (`npm test` locally on `f82cbe3`: 4277 tests, 4272 pass, 0 fail, 5 skipped). One caveat: the PR rollup read at merge time showed an empty conclusion for that check, so I merged on the run's own `success` status.

**Ledger**
1. *Post-merge `test:baseline` on clean main (inside).* Done. Clean `main` @ `d8d186c`, Harbour `d7ceb373`: `npm run test:baseline` (unit tier) exit 0; `npm run test:baseline -- --tier system` exit 0, 127 tests, 127 pass. `observation-feed` (both tests) and `tap1-openrouter` are `pass`; no known-red line is printed. Limits: same host, one run.
2. *`recent` side of the recency oracle (inside).* Settled by the stated limit, as review recorded: in this harness `recent` is always empty, so the `!withinDay` branch is exercised only as an oracle over whatever the feed holds. Harbour's own LIN-3983 unit test covers that side; no clock hack added.
3. *LIN-4188 close (inside).* Closed Done with the baseline output above.
4. *Outside: Harbour's stale "running-only split" comments.* Searched for an existing ticket (`/search`, relations): none. Filed LIN-4230 (Harbour, `routes/dashboard-feed.js` ~285 and ~727), priority level 1 with reason on the ticket, label Improvement + kind:follow-up, related to this ticket.

**Deploy:** none. This is a test/docs change in Simple Dispatcher with no runtime deploy, so there were no post-deploy steps beyond the baseline check above.

**Housekeeping:** LIN-4188 closed. Archive: pre-prune snapshot captured and verified (identical description, 17,599 chars, 2026-11-04T17:47Z). Prune: the discharged Implementation Plan section is replaced with a stub (the `Implementation Plan` heading, `fits one session` and `plan-review due: no` kept word for word); Problem, Acceptance, Anchors and the scope decision are untouched. `bug` label kept.
